elements.element: No minimum purchase / volume / take-or-pay commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment."

elements.element: Fees payable only for services ordered
elements.evidence: "obliged to pay only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage (actual use)
Commitment expressly limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: Redline eliminates any commitment; no 12-month-term commitment language appears in 2.1.
No notice-based reduction mechanic in the rendered clause; only "Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment."

elements.element: Shortfall handled by true-up rather than penalty
elements.evidence: No true-up mechanic; clause simply states pay "only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form or actually used."

offending_extra_words: Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment.
reasons: Preferred level is fully satisfied: the take-or-pay obligation is removed and Fees are expressly limited to Services ordered under a signed Order Form or actually used, matching the preferred position that fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Fallback elements (12-month-limited commitment, 30-day reduction right, true-up instead of penalty) are absent, but that is because the locked target is preferred and no commitment exists at all; the fallback is a separate, lesser bargain and is not required here.

Minimality fails on the official gate: operation 1 changed-character ratio 1.070 exceeds the 0.600 limit, i.e. a full-clause rewrite where a shorter operative edit (or a targeted deletion of the take-or-pay obligation anchored to surrounding unchanged text) would suffice.

The affirmative negative covenant "Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment" duplicates Vendor's existing acknowledgement in 12.3 that Customer has made no "minimum-volume" commitment; the payment-scope sentence alone would carry the preferred position.
Intent is preserved: Section 12.3 is untouched, the contradiction with 12.3 is cured, and the clause uses only defined terms ("Services", "Order Form") with no dangling mechanic.
Suggested tightening: keep only "Customer is obliged to pay only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form or actually used." in place of the take-or-pay sentence to pass the minimality gate.
